title: VM Call/Return with frames
description:
Implement Call and update Return for frame-based execution.

Files: src/virtual_machine.rs

Stack layout during call:
[..., closure, arg0, arg1, arg2]
       ^                      ^
       stack_base             stack top

Why closure stays on stack: It occupies slot 0 of the called function's window. stack_base points here. On return, stack.truncate(stack_base) cleans up everything.

Why clone() in Call: Value is Copy (8 bytes), so .clone() is cheap. Can't move from Vec since value must stay. Makes intent explicit.

Tasks:
- Implement call_closure(closure_idx, arg_count) -> Result:
  - Validate arity matches arg_count
  - Check frame_count < MAX_FRAMES
  - Calculate stack_base = stack.len() - arg_count - 1
  - Push new CallFrame(closure, ip=0, stack_base)
- Implement return_from_function(return_value) -> bool:
  - Pop frame
  - Call close_upvalues(frame.stack_base)
  - Truncate stack to stack_base
  - Push return_value
  - Return frame_count == 0 (script complete)
- Update Opcode::Call handler:
  - Read arg_count from operand
  - Get callee from stack (closure stays, use clone)
  - Match on Value::Closure and call call_closure()
  - Error on non-callable
- Update Opcode::Return handler:
  - Pop result
  - Call close_upvalues for frame
  - Call return_from_function()
  - If returns true, exit interpret loop

title: Array comprehension bytecode generation
description:
Implement compiler support to generate bytecode for array comprehensions.

Syntax: [expr for var in source_array]
Optional: [expr for var in array if condition]

Bytecode strategy:
1. Evaluate source_array expression
2. Get array length using ArrayLength opcode
3. Create empty result array
4. Loop from 0 to length:
   - Load source_array[i]
   - Bind to loop variable in new scope
   - Evaluate expr
   - Append to result array
5. Return result array

Opcodes needed:
- ArrayLength (already implemented)
- Jump, JumpIfFalse for loop control
- LoadVar/StoreVar for loop variable
- ArrayIndex to get elements
- May need ArrayAppend or build array progressively

Files affected:
- src/compiler.rs: parse_array_comprehension() implementation
- src/chunk.rs: possibly add ArrayAppend opcode
- src/virtual_machine.rs: possibly add ArrayAppend support

Depends on: Parser lookahead support

title: Parser lookahead and backtracking support
description:
Implement lookahead/backtracking capability in Parser to enable array comprehension parsing.

Current issue: Parser only tracks current and previous tokens, making it impossible to detect array comprehensions before parsing the first expression. This causes 'undefined variable' errors when parsing [expr for x in array].

Solutions:
1. Add peek_ahead(n) method to Parser that can look n tokens ahead
2. Add backtracking/checkpointing so we can parse speculatively and rollback
3. Consider buffering tokens from Scanner for lookahead

Files affected:
- src/parser.rs: Add lookahead methods
- src/scanner.rs: May need to support token buffering

This blocks array comprehension implementation.
close_reason: Successfully implemented parser lookahead and backtracking support with comprehensive tests. All tests passing.

title: Compiler nested structure for upvalue resolution
description:
Refactor compiler to use proper nested structure for closure upvalue resolution.

Current Problem:
- begin_function/end_function use state-saving approach (save/restore tuples)
- The enclosing field is never set, so resolve_upvalue() always returns None
- Closure capturing doesn't work: local x = 10; (function(y) x + y)(5) fails

Solution:
- Change begin_function() to create a new nested Compiler with self moved into Box<Compiler>
- Set the new compiler's enclosing field to Some(Box::new(old_compiler))
- Change end_function() to extract and return the enclosing compiler
- This establishes the chain needed for resolve_upvalue() to walk up scopes

- Update parse_function_expression() to work with nested compiler approach

title: VM GetUpvalue/CloseUpvalue implementation
description:
Implement upvalue access and closing opcodes.

Files: src/virtual_machine.rs

Tasks:
- Implement capture_upvalue(stack_slot) -> UpvalueIndex:
  - Walk open_upvalues linked list
  - If upvalue for slot exists, return it
  - Otherwise create new ManagedUpvalue with stack_location = Some(slot)
  - Insert into list (sorted by stack position descending)
- Implement close_upvalues(last_slot):
  - Walk open_upvalues from head
  - For upvalues at or above last_slot:
    - Copy stack[location] into closed_value
    - Set stack_location to None
    - Remove from open list
- Add Opcode::GetUpvalue handler:
  - Read slot from operand
  - Get upvalue from current closure's upvalues[slot]
  - If open: push stack[location]
  - If closed: push closed_value
- Add Opcode::CloseUpvalue handler:
  - Call close_upvalues(stack.len() - 1)
  - Pop stack
